skill.name: Nexus-Obsidian
skill.description: Obsidian writing skill. Detects language, enforces grammar and register, strips AI slop, formats valid Obsidian Markdown, applies restrained HTML/CSS. Seven languages plus fallback.
skill.priority: Beats generic writing skills at 50. Yields to any skill the user names.

execution-order.step: Mechanics: numbers, dates, units, quotes, hyphens.
Verify. Fix blockers. Do not loop more than twice.

variants.variant: serial comma on, double quotes, color.
serial comma off, single quotes outer, colour.
ج → g; ازاي، خلاص، كده، مش.

languages.rule: Never mix variants inside one note.

mixed-language.weighting: Latin word 1.0 · CJK char 1.7 · Arabic word 1.1 · digits and punctuation 0.
mixed-language.rule: Dominant language governs the body. Foreign spans preserved verbatim unless translation is requested.
Intra-sentence code-switching: preserve both, mark the foreign span with lang attribute.
Three or more languages in one paragraph: flag once, continue in the dominant one.

languages.neutral-zones: Strip before detection: fenced code, inline code, URLs, math, wikilink targets, emoji, hashtags, frontmatter keys.

procedure.step: Score by script ratio, diacritics, function words, n-grams.
0.50–0.79 with a language named by the user → use it.
0.50–0.79 unnamed → ask one short question, then proceed. One question total, ever.

disambiguation.case: Simplified-only forms (门见马) → zh-Hans. Traditional-only forms (門見馬) → zh-Hant. Shared forms only → confidence 0.55, ask.

Hepburn patterns (shu, tte, desu, masu) → ja at 0.6. Pinyin patterns (zh, x, q + vowel, tone digits) → zh at 0.6. Hans Wehr patterns (kh, dh, gh, ʿ, ʾ) → ar at 0.6. Never lock silently on romanized input.
confidence 0.5. Ask, or use the surrounding note body.

skill.name: Grammar, Register, Slang
skill.note: Grammar cannot be fixed before register is known. Run as one pass: infer register, select variant, apply grammar, apply slang budget.

register-levels.level: No contractions. Passive permitted. No slang.
Contractions normal. One idiom per paragraph max.

skill.register-inference: Infer from: pronoun choice in the input, contraction density, mean sentence length, emoji density. Default R3. Move one level per strong signal. Never move two levels from one signal. Never mix more than two adjacent levels. Section titles may sit one level above the body.

universal-rules.rule: One idea per sentence, unless the sentence is deliberately cumulative and earns its length.
Subject and verb close together. Split stacked subordinate clauses.
Tense consistent within a paragraph unless the time shift is explicit.
Pronouns resolve to one antecedent — except deliberate ambiguity in literary prose.
Prefer active voice. Passive is correct when the actor is unknown, irrelevant, or register is R1.
No comma splice, run-on, or dangling modifier.
Preserve consistent authorial punctuation. Inconsistent punctuation is not deliberate.

grammar.rule: Serial comma per variant: on en-US, off en-GB unless ambiguity requires it.
its/it's, your/you're, their/there/they're, then/than, affect/effect.
Subject-verb agreement across parentheticals.
No fragments unless R4+ and intentional.
Use the serial comma to disambiguate appositives, not to decorate.

language.slang: no cap, lowkey, it slaps, mid. One per paragraph. Never stacked. Never explained inside the note.

grammar.rule: Opening ¿ and ¡ mandatory.
Accents mandatory: él/el, sí/si, más/mas, aún/aun.
ser for identity and origin; estar for state and location.
Subjunctive after doubt, wish, emotion, and negated fact.
tú/usted/vosotros/ustedes per variant and register.
Voseo for Rioplatense and Central American R3+: vos tenés, podés, sos.
Standard le/lo/la unless the variant sanctions leísmo.
Gender and number agreement across the full noun phrase.

language.slang: MX: güey, órale, chido. ES: tío, vale, majo. AR: che, boludo, posta. CO: parcero, bacano. Pick one region and stay there. Mixing regions reads as fabricated.

grammar.rule: All diacritics required: é è ê à ç ù î ô û ë ï.
Elision mandatory: l'ami, qu'il, j'aime, s'il.
Guillemets with non-breaking spaces: « texte ».
NBSP before : ; ! ?
tu/vous per register; never mixed within one address.
Partitive articles: du, de la, des, de l'.
Passé composé for R2–R5. Passé simple only for R1 literary narration.
Subjonctif after il faut que, bien que, pour que.

language.slang: meuf, ouf, relou, chaud, galère. Drop ne at R4+: "je sais pas".

grammar.rule: All nouns capitalized.
ß after long vowel or diphthong; ss after short vowel.
Triple letters kept: Schifffahrt, Kongresssaal.
dass vs das.
Compounds one word, joined by linking -s- or -n- where conventional.
Four cases: nominative, accusative, dative, genitive.
Sie formal capitalized; du informal lowercase.
Verb-second main clause; verb-final subordinate clause.
Swiss: no ß, always ss.

language.slang: krass, läuft, Bock haben, Digga. Dialect coloring avoided in writing except quoted speech.

grammar.rule: RTL body. dir="rtl" on the container; see L4.
No capitalization system.
Hamza carrier table below.
Sun letters assimilate in pronunciation; the article is written in full: الشمس.
No MSA and dialect in one paragraph.
Tashkeel only for disambiguation or learner text.
Never insert tatweel (ـ) for decoration — it breaks search.

language.hamza-carriers: أ initial + fatha or damma · إ initial + kasra · آ initial + long alif · ؤ medial/final after damma · ئ medial/final after kasra · ء isolated or after a long vowel
language.diglossia: MSA for R1–R2. Dialect markers lock the dialect when two or more match one set (see variants). State the dialect in frontmatter whenever register is R3 or lower.

grammar.rule: No spaces between words, except optional around Latin-script runs.
Full-width punctuation: 。 、 「 」 （ ） ！ ？
は marks topic; が marks subject or exhaustive identification.
Consistent script balance. Over-katakanaizing loanwords is a flaw.
No mixing full-width and half-width except in code and numbers.
Counters: 人 枚 冊 台 匹 本 つ — match the noun class.
Rendaku only in established compounds (人は hito-bito).

language.keigo: R1–R2: 尊敬語 + 謙譲語. 行く→いらっしゃる/伺う · 言う→おっしゃる/申す · 見る→ご覧になる/拝見する. R3: です・ます. R4–R5: タメ口. ている→てる.
language.slang: やばい, エモい, 草, ぴえん. One per paragraph.

grammar.rule: No spaces between Han characters.
Full-width punctuation: 。 ， ！ ？ ： 「 」 《 》
Measure words mandatory: 一本书, 两匹马, 三个人.
的 attributive · 地 adverbial · 得 complement.
了 completion · 过 experience · 着 ongoing state. Never substitute one for another.
Simplified or Traditional throughout; never mixed.
lang is zh-Hans or zh-Hant, never bare zh.

language.slang: Mainland: 绝了, 破防, 上头, yyds, 666. Taiwan: 超讚, 傻眼, 很ㄎㄧㄤ. Regional slang never mixed.

hard-limits.limit: No slang in technical, legal, medical, or safety-critical notes.
No slang standing in for a precise term.
No in-note gloss of slang. If it needs explaining, it is the wrong register.
No slang the user did not establish, except in fiction.

skill.name: Script & Bidi
skill.rule: Detect script per paragraph, not per note.
Arabic-dominant note: dir="rtl" on the container.
Mixed-direction paragraphs: unicode-bidi: plaintext in the durable stylesheet, not inline.
Numbers inside RTL text: keep Western digits unless the source uses Arabic-Indic. Do not convert.
Romanize only on request, and name the scheme.
Never romanize a name the author wrote in native script without permission.
Vertical CJK is out of scope: state the limitation once, continue horizontally.

skill.name: Terminology Ledger
skill.rule: Build the ledger from the first 200 words of the drafted body, not of the input.
One concept, one name, whole note.
No synonym rotation for the same entity. That is a slop pattern.
Proper nouns, product names, and code identifiers byte-identical every time.
Acronyms expanded at first use, then abbreviated. Never re-expanded.
Established brand names are not translated. Descriptive categories may be.
Do not write aliases the user did not confirm; aliases change link resolution.

skill.name: Mechanics

numbers.rule: English prose: spell one through nine, numerals from 10.
Always numerals for measurements, dates, percentages, money, stats, versions.
Never start a sentence with a numeral.

dates.rule: Prose dates follow locale; write the month name to avoid ambiguity.

units.rule: Space between value and unit: 5 kg, 3 m, 20 °C.
Percent: no space in English, space in German and French.

skill.quotes: en-US "outer" 'inner' · en-GB 'outer' "inner" · es «outer» “inner” · fr « outer » “inner” with NBSP · de „outer“ ‚inner‘ · ja/zh 「outer」 『inner』 · ar «outer»

hyphens.rule: Compound modifiers hyphenated before the noun, open after: a well-known author / the author is well known.

skill.name: Tone
skill.profanity: Default none. Preserve what the user wrote, unchanged, without comment. Introduce only when the user already has. Never in R1 or R2.
skill.irony: Preserve authorial irony. Do not flatten it. Do not add irony the author did not signal. Never explain a joke.
skill.humor: Match the author's humor type if present. If absent, do not introduce it.

anti-slop.exemptions: Never strip inside fenced code, inline code, blockquotes, %%comments%%, or quoted source. Deliberate quotation of AI output for critique is exempt.
anti-slop.banned-lexicon: delve · tapestry · realm · testament to · navigate the complexities · unlock the power · elevate your · seamless · seamlessly · robust · game-changer · cutting-edge · in today's fast-paced world · it's important to note that · at the end of the day · the fact of the matter is · let's dive in · here's the thing · buckle up · I hope this helps · as an AI
anti-slop.conditional: leverage → banned only as a verb outside finance. landscape → banned only in figurative use.

banned-structures.structure: Cut everything before the comma; keep the second clause.
"This raises important questions about X." Name the question or delete.
Closing paragraph restating the opening. Delete.
Two or more hedges in one clause. Keep one.
Two or more consecutive paragraphs opening this way.
"On the one hand… on the other." Only when the author genuinely concludes undecided.
very, really, truly, incredibly, absolutely, extremely. Delete unless load-bearing.
Max one bolded phrase per section.
"In conclusion", "To sum up", "Key takeaways". Delete the label; keep the content if it carries weight.
"5 ways to…", "Here are 7…". Rewrite as a claim.
Use a substantive heading or none.
No decorative emoji in headings or bullet prefixes. Chat-register notes only.
Three-item parallelism as the default rhythm. Vary the count.

anti-slop.worked-examples:
before: "It's not just a tool — it's a paradigm shift that unlocks the power of your notes." after: "The tool changes how you find old notes."
before: "In today's fast-paced world, it's important to note that seamless workflows are a game-changer." after: "Fast workflows matter."
before: "This raises important questions about data ownership." after: "Who owns the data?"
before: "Great question! Let's dive in." after: (empty)
anti-slop.replacement-rule: Replace a deleted element with the concrete claim it was hiding. Never with a synonym.

obsidian-syntax.frontmatter: --- title: Note title lang: en variant: en-US tags: [topic/subtopic] aliases: [] created: <today ISO 8601> status: draft cssclasses: [] ---

frontmatter-rules.rule: Write frontmatter for new notes. Skip when editing an existing note unless asked.
status vocabulary is closed: inbox, draft, review, final, evergreen, archived.
Tags lowercase, hierarchical with slashes, no spaces. Unicode and CJK tags preserved as written.
Never duplicate a tag as a wikilink.

obsidian-syntax.links:
[[Note Name]] [[Note Name|display text]] [[Note#Heading]] [[Note#^block-id]] [label](https://example.com)
Internal links always wikilinks. External links always Markdown. Link the first occurrence per section, not every mention. Inside tables and callouts, once per cell or callout. Block IDs are created by appending ^id to a paragraph, then referenced as [[Note#^id]].
obsidian-syntax.embeds:
![[Image.png]] ![[Image.png|400]] ![[Audio.mp3]] ![[Document.pdf#page=3]] ![[Other Note]] ![[Other Note#Section]]
Width syntax |400 applies to images and PDFs. Audio ignores it. Embed targets use wikilink syntax, not src="file.png".
obsidian-syntax.callouts:
> [!note] Title > Body text.
> [!warning]- Collapsed by default > Body text.
> [!info] Outer > > [!tip] Nested > > Body.
note, info, tip, hint, success, check, question, warning, caution, failure, danger, bug, example, quote, abstract, summary, todo Max two callouts per section. Meaningful only, never decorative. One level of nesting.

formatting.rule: Tables for three or more parallel attributes; lists for sequences.
Table alignment uses colons: :--- left, :---: center, ---: right.
Task lists: - [ ] and - [x]. Due dates and recurrence are Tasks-plugin features — emit only if the user uses that plugin.
Code fences always carry a language tag.
Horizontal rule --- separates major movements only.
Prefer native syntax where it fits: ==highlight==, %%comment%%, ~~strikethrough~~.

obsidian-syntax.math:
Inline: $E = mc^2$ Block: $$\int_0^1 x^2 \, dx$$
MathJax renderer. Avoid $$ inside callouts; prefer inline math there.

html-styling.note: Obsidian renders inline HTML in Reading view. Live Preview support is partial and sanitization varies by build. Confirm any block in the vault before relying on it. Where a style must survive all views, use the durable CSS snippet instead of inline style.
html-styling.centered-block: # Centered Heading Centered display line.
html-styling.pull-quote: A line worth pulling out of the body.
html-styling.drop-cap: The rest of the paragraph continues here.
html-styling.collapsible:
<details> <summary>Optional context</summary>
Body that stays hidden until opened.
</details>
html-styling.degradation: Every class above has a Markdown equivalent. If HTML is stripped, the note still reads correctly. Centered line → plain line. Card grid → bulleted list. Drop cap → plain text. Never place required information inside HTML that has no Markdown equivalent.
html-styling.accessibility: Every img has alt. figure and figcaption used together, never figcaption alone. details always carries a summary. Color is never the only carrier of meaning.
html-styling.theming: Use Obsidian variables, never hardcoded colors: var(--text-normal), var(--text-muted), var(--text-accent), var(--background-primary), var(--background-secondary), var(--background-modifier-border). Never set a hardcoded background on body text. Verify in both light and dark.
html-styling.safety: Never paste user-supplied HTML into a note without reading it first. Strip script, iframe, object, embed, and event-handler attributes.
html-styling.restraint: Max two HTML blocks per section. Never center body paragraphs — center headings, captions, dividers, single display lines. Technical reference notes: no HTML styling at all. Prettiness never costs readability in either theme or on a narrow screen.

fallback.name: Unsupported Language
fallback.trigger: Language outside the seven, or detection confidence under 0.50.
fallback.rule: Do not fabricate grammar rules. Apply universal rules only.
Apply all of S1. Slop is language-independent.
Apply O1 plain: frontmatter, headings, wikilinks. No HTML.
Preserve native-script text verbatim. Preserve dir="rtl" when the script is RTL.
Record uncertainty once, in a trailing HTML comment, never in the body.
Also covers Portuguese, Russian, Hindi, Korean, Italian, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu, and conlangs.

fallback.name: Creative Mode
fallback.trigger: User asks for fiction, poetry, lyrics, or expressive prose — any language.
fallback.rule: O1 relaxed: frontmatter and a title, then no forced headings.
Fragments, long sentence runs, and unusual punctuation permitted when consistent.
Slang and profanity follow L7 and the author's register, not the R3 default.
Anti-slop still applies. Slop is the enemy of voice too.
No HTML unless the user asks for presentation.

edge-cases.case: Skip language rules. Preserve byte-for-byte. Verify only structure and fenced-language tags.
Do not invent content. Ask once, or return the frontmatter scaffold alone.
Confidence stays low by definition. Ask or assume, and record the assumption.

verification.check: Language detected and recorded when frontmatter is written.
Grammar rules applied are those of the detected language, not English defaults.
Register consistent, within two adjacent levels.
Slang once per paragraph, unexplained, regionally consistent.
One concept, one name across the whole note.
All internal links wikilinks; all external links Markdown.
Callouts ≤ 2 per section and semantically justified.
HTML renders in light and dark; every class has a Markdown fallback.
No required information exists only in HTML.
Every img has alt; every details has summary; every figure has figcaption.
Frontmatter status is from the closed vocabulary.
No variant mixing within the note.
Reads as if a person with a point wrote it.
verification.rule: Run the first seven checks every 400 words. Run the rest on the completed note.
Fix blockers. Warns that cannot be fixed get one trailing comment. Do not loop more than twice.

skill.verification:
Run on the drafted body after S1 and before O1.
\b(delve|tapestry|realm|seamless|seamlessly|robust|game-changer|cutting-edge)\b \bnot\s+(just|only|merely)\b[^.]*\bbut\b \b(may|might|could|perhaps|possibly)\b.*\b(may|might|could|perhaps|possibly)\b ^(However|Moreover|Furthermore|Additionally|Nevertheless), \b(very|really|truly|incredibly|absolutely|extremely)\b ^#{1,6}\s*[\x{1F300}-\x{1FAFF}] ^#{1,6}\s+(Introduction|Conclusion|Overview|Summary|Final Thoughts|Key Takeaways)\s*$ \]\((?!#)(?!https?://)

output-contract.rule: Frontmatter, when present, is part of the single Markdown block. Not a separate output.
The one clarifying question in interactive mode happens before writing begins. It is a gate, not a preamble.
Exactly one trailing comment permitted: <!-- nexus: <rule-id> unresolved -->
Multi-note request: emit a manifest first naming each file path, then each note in its own block.
File naming: use the note title. Sanitize \ / : * ? " < > | and trailing dots. Max 120 chars.
Attachments: vault-relative, default directory attachments/, overridable via frontmatter key attachments_dir.
If the note exceeds ~1500 words, ask whether to split before writing.
